prometheus.main: {prometheus-queries} to select and transform time-series data. Use a metric name to fetch series, {label-filter} to filter by labels, and range selectors like {range-selector} with functions such as {rate-function} to calculate changes over time. Read more in the {official-prometheus-docs}.

example-1.description: {query} - latest request counter values for only {method} requests from the {service} service

example-2.description: {query} - total request rate grouped by {service}, useful for multi-series charts

postgresql.main: {postgresql-queries}. For time-series charts, return a column named {time-column}, one or more {numeric-column} columns for values, and optionally {string-column} columns such as {service-column} or {environment-column} to split the result into multiple series. Sort results by {time-column}. Use {select-keyword} to read data, {where-keyword} to filter rows, {group-by-keyword} to aggregate, and macros/template variables for time filtering and bucketing. For PostgreSQL syntax, see the official {select-keyword} {docs-link}.

main-placeholders.postgresql-queries: PostgreSQL queries should return chart-friendly columns

example-1.title: Single series
example-1.query: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(time, $__interval), AVG(duration_seconds) AS avg_duration_seconds FROM deployments WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

example-2.title: Multiple series
example-2.query: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(time, $__interval), AVG(duration_seconds) AS avg_duration_seconds, service FROM deployments WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1, 3 ORDER BY 1, 3
example-2.description: Returns one separate series per {service-column}, each showing {result} over time
